chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not swear by Allah, neither truthfully nor falsely,'
'for indeed He, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And do not make Allah an excuse for your oaths."'

key_terms.تَحْلِفُوا: To swear/take an oath, invoking a sacred name as witness
key_terms.عُرْضَةً: An obstacle, target, or barrier; here meaning making Allah a habitual shield or excuse invoked in oaths

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden to swear by Allah in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits swearing by Allah in all circumstances — whether in truth or falsehood — citing Quran 2:224 as the divine basis for this ruling. This hadith addresses early Muslim communities who were accustomed to invoking Allah's name in oaths; the Imam teaches that habitually swearing by God's name diminishes reverence for the Divine. The Quranic verse (2:224) was revealed in the context of oaths that prevented people from charitable acts, but its principle extends to casual or frequent invocation of God's name in oaths.
